findings.title: A due box's withdraw reads the five-minute quiet rule before its Koios reads and giveme.my, never again before its submit, so a send that starts in between is followed seconds later
findings.scenario: A box is due and ripe, and nothing was sent for ten minutes. At T0 the alarm's run reaches withdrawDueNow, and the quiet check passes (sends() finds nothing within 5 min). It then waits on the network before it sends: made() may ask Koios tx_info for a box no record accounts for, withdrawOne reads the pool's mix_logic account_info through the shared Koios queue (a 45 s timeout, 429 holds up to 60 s), the withdraw is built and proved, and giveme.my is asked to sign (20 s timeout). That takes seconds, or up to a minute when Koios is holding. Meanwhile one of three senders goes out. (a) The user presses Send on a Make public, and its writeAhead stamps its inputs spent at T0+3 s. (b) Home's 15 s poll pumps a payment's waiting part. (c) A connected site's submitTx goes through the connector. None of them takes Lovejoin's turn. The withdraw is submitted at T0+6 s, a few seconds after the other transaction. It never looks at sends() again. So Koios or the data layer, and giveme.my, see a box come back into a fresh register seconds after another of this wallet's transactions from the same IP. That is the pairing the rule exists for: 'a withdraw minutes after a payment says both are one owner's' (lovejoin.ts:1691). privacy.md:440 says the way back follows 'rules that keep its way back from lining up with anything else the wallet does'. No money moves wrongly. A box's privacy rests on its way back not lining up with the user's other sends.
findings.since: d74677a9 (2026-09-27, privacy review §3.1, before 1.0.0; the check's line from d5972867, M10). The window widened with 7a8c9eeb (1.8.1), which added the per-withdraw account_info read
findings.evidence: lovejoin.ts:6898-6911: the comment says 'Nor right after something else the wallet sent: in the same run (the next takes it), or within QUIET_AFTER_SEND_MS'; the code is `const { sent, forgotten } = await this.deps.wallet.sends(); if (since !== undefined && sent >= since) return []; … const push = quiet(now, sent, forgotten); if (push && pushes < QUIET_PUSHES) { … moveDue … return []; }`. Then come the network waits. :6921-6925 `const { origins, untold } = await this.made(network, [box]);` (made → lookUp → Koios). :6938 `return [await this.withdrawOne(network, read, box, { unlocked, due: time, … })]`. In withdrawOne: :7572 `const rewards = rewardsField(await this.rewardsIn(network, [pool]));` (rewardsIn :4651 → readRewards → koios.accountInfo), then the WASM build, then :7637 `const collateral = await this.deps.collateral(network).witness(built.txCbor);` (collateral.ts:11 TIMEOUT_MS = 20_000). After the network calls, only two checks run: :7643 the hash, and :7644 `if (unlocked !== undefined && (await wallet.unlockedAt()) !== unlocked) throw … lj.lockedWhileBuilding`. The unlock is checked again after the waits (L11/F6), but the quiet rule isn't. Then :7684 `rememberSpent(…)` and :7692 `submitted = await koios.submitTx(bytes);`. The senders that run alongside without Lovejoin's turn: handlers.ts:239 `if (ctx.parts) unawaited(ctx, ctx.parts.pump(ctx.network));` (Home's pending-tx poll) → parts.ts step → script-spend send → pending.ts:610 `rememberSpent(session, s.network, bytes, before.at, record.account)`; a page's Send takes the same path; dapp.ts:2648 `rememberSiteSpent(session, bytes)` after a site's submit. lastSpentAt counts each of them, but only when it is read. The withdraw's own resend does it in the right order: settleWithdrawing reads `onChain` (network) first and then resends() → `this.deps.wallet.sends()` (:7892-7895) just before its submit. runs.ts only orders the alarm's own sends (withdraws last). It doesn't cover a page's or a site's. Tests: lovejoin-withdraw-submit.test.ts:246 and unlock-waits.test.ts:113 pin a send made before the run. Nothing drives a send made while the withdraw is being built. A verifier test, modelled on lovejoin-withdraw-submit.test.ts:178 ('a withdraw built across a lock and an unlock'): wrap t.collateral.fetch so that before answering it does `await t.wallet.withKeys(() => rememberSpent(t.session, "preprod", otherTxBytes, t.clock.now))` (a Send that went while giveme.my answered). Then call `lovejoin.withdrawDue("preprod", false, t.clock.now)` and expect t.koios.submitted unchanged and the due time pushed by at least QUIET_PUSH_MS[0]. Today the withdraw is submitted. No command run (finder).
findings.fix: Read the quiet rule again just before the withdraw is kept and sent, as the unlock already is (7644). In withdrawOne, for the runner's withdraws (not withdrawNow or Bring every box back, which the user asked for), check after giveme.my answers whether `sends().sent` is past the time of the first check, or past `since`. If it is, put the due time back with a quiet push (the same moveDue as 6906-6910) and send nothing. Its giveme.my witness is thrown away. The class is every automatic send that passes a timing gate and then waits on the network before it submits. Lovejoin's withdraw re-checks the unlock but not the quiet rule (this one). The sessions runner re-checks neither (x4#2). The withdraw's resend already does both in order (settleWithdrawing → resends).
findings.known_check: Searched backlog.md and docs/archive/plans/*.md (independent-review, privacy-review §3.1, final-review F6/F8, chunk-16) for quiet, QUIET_AFTER, 'right after the wallet', 'after a send', M10, L8, L11, F6 and 'while Koios answered'. What I found: the rule's origin (§3.1, d74677a); M10, where a lock forgot the last send; L8 and F8, where resends and let-go payments now count as sends; F6, the unlock checked again after the resend's tx_status; and the deliberate 'after 3 pushes it goes anyway'. Nothing covers a send that starts while a new withdraw is being built.

findings.title: The sessions runner checks the unlock's wait once, before a step's Minswap and Koios calls: a lock and unlock during them sends the step seconds after the unlock
findings.scenario: A swap that runs itself has landed its funding, and its order is due. The alarm's run (run = 'run') reaches act at T. go() calls waits(), which finds no recent unlock and returns false. order() then asks Minswap for a route and for build-tx, and reads the cancels' reference rows from Koios: several seconds, or up to a minute under a Koios 429 hold. During that time the user presses Lock and then unlocks with the password. No key is used while it's locked, so nothing fails. When Minswap answers, inspect, signAndSend and sendRecorded run under the new unlock, and the order is submitted seconds after it. A step found at or after an unlock waits a fresh 2–20 min draw (privacy review §3.1, independent review L10–L12). A connected site that polls isEnabled sees the unlock and then the session's order land right after it. The same goes for a cancel after Stop and for a return, direct or through Lovejoin: bringBack → buildBack's pool reads and crossCheck → recordChain, then its first transaction. runs.ts:33-36 promises the opposite: 'What each service sends checks the unlock time again itself (wallet.ts unlockedAt)'. Lovejoin's withdraws do (lovejoin.ts:7644, 7869); the sessions runner doesn't. No money moves wrongly: a timing rule is skipped.
findings.since: d74677a9 (2026-09-27, privacy review §3.1: go/waits); 61db0436 (L10–L12) kept the single check; before 1.0.0, in every tagged release
findings.evidence: runs.ts:33-36: 'A run is long … the wallet can lock and unlock again while it goes on: the rest of it is then the unlock's run, which sends nothing (independent review L11). What each service sends checks the unlock time again itself (wallet.ts unlockedAt).' runs.ts:78-81 and :94 check `relocked()` once per network, before sessions.runAll, not inside a step. sessions.ts:3806-3807 is `const go = async (send) => { if (!(await this.waits(network, s, run))) await send(); };`, and :3940-3942 waits() reads `const unlocked = await this.deps.wallet.unlockedAt();` once. order() runs from :4136: routeOf (Minswap estimate), :4167 `const txCbor = await minswap.buildTx(address, min, asked, avoid);`, then inspect (Koios reference reads), then :4175 `await this.signAndSend(network, built);`. signAndSend (:4473) signs in withKeys and goes straight to sendRecorded, then :5553 `await this.submit(network, bytes, txHash);`. grep finds unlockedAt in sessions.ts only at :3942, so nothing compares it again after waits. The lock's wipe of session storage doesn't stop the step: order(), inspect and signAndSend need nothing kept in session storage, and the book is sealed in local storage. Contrast lovejoin.ts:7644, 'sending a withdraw built across a lock and an unlock', which is tested by lovejoin-withdraw-submit.test.ts:178. unlock-waits.test.ts:367-460 ('a swap's step at the unlock') tests only a step found at or after the unlock, never one in flight across it. A verifier test in that harness (signing(t), funded(t, sessions)): wrap t.minswap.fetch so that, on build-tx, it first does `await t.wallet.lock(); t.clock.now += 20_000; await t.wallet.unlock(PASSWORD);`. Then call `await sessions.runAll("preprod")` and expect no new submit of SWAP_TX, with auto.waitsUntil at least the unlock plus UNLOCK_WAIT_MS[0]. Today the order is submitted. No command run (finder).
findings.fix: Carry the unlock time waits() read into the step, and check it again just before each of the runner's submits: sendRecorded's submit for swaps, cancels and returns, and the first send of a chain recordChain/pump starts in the step. On a change, record the step to wait for the new unlock's draw (set unlockWait/unlockDrawn as waits does) and send nothing, as lovejoin.ts:7644 refuses a withdraw built across an unlock. 'asked' runs (Try now, Stop, Refresh) stay exempt, as waits makes them. The class is every automatic send that passes a timing gate and then waits on the network. See x4#1 for the withdraw's quiet rule. Parts are safe from this one: a lock wipes their kept copies, so send() refuses them.
findings.known_check: Searched backlog.md and docs/archive/plans/*.md for 'lock and an unlock', 'across a lock', 'while Koios answered', 'locked while', L10, L11, L12, F6 and §3.1. guards.stops: writeAhead: a submit cut off by a lock, a closed browser or a stopped worker is forgotten, and the payment is built and paid again. It is watched as maybe sent and sealed before Koios is asked; one that can't be sealed isn't sent (:621)
restoreNow: a maybe-sent payment that a lock wiped is put back with its UTxOs held, and its first resend waits RESEND_MS from now, so nothing goes at the moment of unlock (L9)
settleMaybeSent: a new payment built or sent beside one that may still go through (paying twice), across a lock too
guards.test: tests/maybe-sent.test.ts 'comes back maybe sent, holds its UTxOs back, and stops new payments until it lands'

guards.stops: A kept review sent on another network, or one another window overwrote: refused as stale, after refuseSent, so a page that missed the answer never builds a second payment
guards.test: tests/transfer.test.ts 'refuses to send anything but the reviewed transaction'

guards.stops: A withdraw built across a lock and an unlock: not sent, its due time kept for the new unlock's draw (L11)
guards.test: tests/lovejoin-withdraw-submit.test.ts:178 'a withdraw built across a lock and an unlock'

guards.stops: The quiet rule: no withdraw in a run that sent anything else, or within 5 minutes of the wallet's own send. It is read only before the withdraw's network calls (x4#1)
waits: a swap's or a return's step found at an unlock goes out at once; it waits a fresh draw. Read only before the step's network calls (x4#2)
relocked: a run spanning a lock and an unlock goes on as a normal run. Each later network's part becomes the unlock's run, which sends nothing (L11)
Two background runs at once (the alarm and an unlock), which would send two withdraws or steps seconds apart
funded(): a site handed a session whose funding in parts is short. It is checked from storage on every call, so the rule holds after a worker restart drops watchFunding's in-memory wait
guards.test: site-funding tests by name (tests/site-funding-seen.test.ts), not opened

guards.stops: Remove wallet, while unlocked, under a maybe-sent payment, open sessions, a chain being sent, a maybe-sent public mix or parts still to go, without a second yes
sendRecorded: a session transaction, with its summary, is recorded before its submit, so a lock or a stopped worker mid-submit leaves it looked for, never taken for unsent
Two pumps at once (the alarm and Home's poll) sending one waiting part twice
guards.test: tests/parts-send-review-fixes.test.ts 'runs one pump at a time'

guards.stops: A part refused because its parent isn't seen yet (a rollback, or giveme.my or Koios behind) stopping the rest: it waits GIVEME_BEHIND_MS from when the parent was seen
Any key use past the auto-lock deadline: load() locks first, so a missed alarm or a slow network call can't sign after the deadline
guards.test: tests/wallet.test.ts auto-lock cases, by name, not opened

guards.stops: After a worker restart, a site's signature or submit asked again blindly: only reads are retried, a signature hears 'nothing was signed', and a submit hears it may have gone

checked_ok: pending.ts's write order in writeAhead (spent stamps, then the kept sentCbor, then the watch, then the sealed copy, then the submit) fails safe wherever a worker stops. A stop before the seal leaves either nothing submitted or a maybe-sent watch that resends the bytes Send asked for. A lock then drops only one that was never submitted.

wallet.ts open()/wipe() fail safe when a stop falls between their writes. Entropy without a lastActivity stamp reads as idle and locks. A missing unlockedAt counts from now. A stop between session.clear() and the restored sends falls back on noteStart's `since`, so the quiet rule still keeps away from the forgotten window.

A background run spanning Remove wallet plus a restore of another phrase: each step re-reads the sealed book and records under the new store key, and sessions.reset clears the scan. withdrawOne's unlockedAt check refuses a withdraw built under the old phrase. What leaks is history writes (notes, e4a#1).

dapp.ts: approvals, watchFunding and fundingReads live in memory, but every rule they enforce is read again from storage by the next call. funded() gives a site a funding in parts only once every part has landed; the bridge's cut-off words cover a signature or a submit that was in flight across a worker restart.

Two pages at once: kept reviews are matched by key, txHash and network; keepParts ties later parts by partHashes and removes leftovers; refuseSent covers a page that missed the answer; Lovejoin's public review holds its reservation until Send. A review another window overwrote is refused as stale and never sent twice.

Account switch mid-flow: readAccount can mix two accounts' reads, but WebAssembly's check_paths refuses the build. Pages re-key on LOCAL_ACCOUNT's change (accounts.tsx onChanged), so a review built for the account left can't be Sent from a live page. writeAhead and the collateral record use the review's account (309#2). handlers.ts refuses a switch while a payment or public mix is on its way.

Network switch mid-flow: every cache, watch, reservation and sent list is per network. send()/move-in submit refuse a kept review of the other network. dapp.ts declines a waiting request of the network left, except a sent funding, which connects on its own network.

Late and rolled-back landings: parts treat a giveme.my or Koios refusal of a child whose parent was just seen as 'behind' for 3 min, which covers a parent dropped by a one- or two-block rollback. pending's mempool() holds a maybe-sent one whose inputs are still unspent. Session funding parts missed at 20 min still hold Disconnect while they may land. The private index seals only below its stable cursor.

ActivityService.update is serialized, and sent() replaces an earlier 'received' entry for the same transaction. A landing the balance noted before Send's history entry is corrected, and classes() then reads the sent entry.

The unlock moment: restoreNow's resentAt, sessions' waits for steps found at an unlock, Lovejoin's unlockDraws and the unlock's run that sends nothing all hold. Parts in session storage are wiped by a lock, so Home's poll (unlock=false) normally finds none at the unlock. The runners' own advance from pages uses now=false, so they keep the unlock's wait.
settleWithdrawing's resend reads its network status first and then the quiet rule (resends) just before its submit: the right order, unlike a new withdraw (x4#1).

Forgot password (locked) can't keep a public mix's maybe record. That is documented in architecture.md:729 and privacy.md:272, and lovejoin.keptMaybe treats another phrase's record as none rather than throwing.
notes: e4a#1 / e6#2, more of the same class (a write made under the phrase whose keys are present when its Koios call returns, not the phrase it began under): (1) pending.ts:773 settleNow → `deps.activity?.sent(w.network, shown(seen), w.summary)` writes a maybe-sent payment's summary into the next phrase's sealed history, when a forced Remove wallet plus a restore lands while its lookFor is out. (2) lovejoin.ts withdrawOne's post-submit `this.deps.activity?.sent(network, pending, back)` (about :7740), and settleWithdrawing's at :7853, write the old phrase's box-back entry into the new phrase's history when the submit or onChain call spans Remove plus a restore. Remove wallet doesn't list a withdraw in flight (atStake). (3) sessions.ts noteLanded and settleReturns, for returns. Same fix: an epoch or pin compared before each sealed write.

E2b's holdWaiting note (parts.ts:341-369), new fact for the backlog's ❓ 'Waiting parts across a lock': parts that holdWaiting remakes after a lock and an unlock during Send's last part go at Home's first pending-tx poll after the unlock. handlers.ts:239 pumps with unlock=false, and Home polls at mount, which breaks privacy review §3.1's 'nothing goes out at the moment of unlock' as well as the parts header's 'a lock means the rest never go'.

Not a finding, for the owner: heldForLovejoin (dapp.ts:1896) is checked when a site's transaction is signed and again at approval, never at submit. A site that got a signature before a public mix started can submit it once the chain is being sent, through the connector's submitTx (which checks nothing) or its own backend. If that transaction spends the account's collateral or the chain's first input, the chain stops after its deposit. The refusals are phase-1 only, so no collateral is lost, but the boxes are left not mixed and Mix again is needed. Through e3a#1's probe a site can also learn when a chain is being sent. A re-check at submitTx would cover only the connector's route.

Corollary of the backlog's ⬜ 'Private spends carry no validity interval': a maybe-sent private payment that is let go as unseen at 20 minutes and lands later has lost its summary with the watch. arrived() then notes its change as 'Received' (a stranger's class, receivedIn) and the payment never appears in the private Activity. Selection is on the safe side: the change is kept apart.

send.ts pay(): the build (one wallet-queue turn, :140) and keep() (its own turn, script-spend.ts keep reading keys.account) are separate. An account switch queued during a long WASM build runs between them, so the review is recorded under the new account while it was signed by the old one. That is harmless today: the page re-keys on the switch, so nothing Sends it, and send() refuses an unknown txHash. A single turn would make submitCollateral's account record (send.ts:102) independent of that.

E3b's note on two connector windows, traced: ask() doesn't await show() and show() has no in-flight guard, so two requests in one tick can open two popups. closeWindow() closes the first that getContexts lists, and windowClosed() with nothing waiting leaves `closing` true while the other popup is open. A later user close of the remaining window, with requests waiting, then shows a new window instead of declining them. That is cosmetic: never declined unseen.

x4#1 and x4#2 are one class: an automatic send whose timing gate (the quiet rule, the unlock's wait) is read before its network waits. Lovejoin's withdraw re-reads the unlock (L11/F6) but not the quiet rule, and the sessions runner re-reads neither. T1 could pin both with the lock-and-unlock-inside-a-fetch pattern that lovejoin-withdraw-submit.test.ts:178 already uses.
